fullPassage: Despite their potential value, urban lakes are often poorly managed and severely degraded. This is because they are, by their very nature, at the “end-of-the-pipe,” often receiving large volumes of wastewater (treated and untreated) and stormwater run-off produced in cities. One particularly severe example is Bellandur Lake in Bengaluru, which often caught fire and produced foam in the past because it received large amounts of untreated wastewater from millions of people living upstream. Decomposition of this organic matter led to a loss of oxygen from the water and a decline in fish and most other animal life. The high levels of decomposition and absence of oxygen also resulted in a huge production of the greenhouse gas methane, a flammable gas that was the likely cause of the fires on the lake surface. The severely degraded state of many urban lakes highlights that current approaches to managing water quality across cities have failed. Not only have city authorities failed to recognise the interconnectedness between urban catchments and lakes, but also the centralised wastewater treatment infrastructure is often highly inadequate, lagging behind rapidly growing populations and particularly ineffective during high rainfall periods, such as the monsoons. In India, lake quality assessment plans are not designed to evaluate the usability of lakes for the multiple benefits they provide, within a timescale that is useful for lake managers. The management of city lakes is divided among different groups, including water supply and sewage services, city departments that handle rainwater, and pollution regulators who mostly focus on industrial waste rather than household wastewater.

❌ ② slight — 미미한 (반대 뉘앙스)
❌ ③ equal — 동등한 (관련 없음)
✅ ④ enormous — 막대한 ←정답
det.tip: a huge production of methane = 메탄의 막대한 발생 → huge = enormous

questions.passage: Despite their potential value, urban lakes are often poorly managed and severely degraded. This is because they are, by their very nature, at the “end-of-the-pipe,” often receiving large volumes of wastewater (treated and untreated) and stormwater run-off produced in cities. One particularly severe example is Bellandur Lake in Bengaluru, which often caught fire and produced foam in the past because it received large amounts of untreated wastewater from millions of people living upstream. Decomposition of this organic matter led to a loss of oxygen from the water and a decline in fish and most other animal life. The high levels of decomposition and absence of oxygen also resulted in a huge production of the greenhouse gas methane, a flammable gas that was the likely cause of the fires on the lake surface. The severely degraded state of many urban lakes highlights that current approaches to managing water quality across cities have failed. Not only have city authorities failed to recognise the interconnectedness between urban catchments and lakes, but also the centralised wastewater treatment infrastructure is often highly inadequate, lagging behind <u>rapidly</u> growing populations and particularly ineffective during high rainfall periods, such as the monsoons. In India, lake quality assessment plans are not designed to evaluate the usability of lakes for the multiple benefits they provide, within a timescale that is useful for lake managers. The management of city lakes is divided among different groups, including water supply and sewage services, city departments that handle rainwater, and pollution regulators who mostly focus on industrial waste rather than household wastewater.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 rapidly와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: rapidly ↔ slowly (빠르게 ↔ 느리게)
det.analysis:
✅ ① slowly — 느리게 ←정답
❌ ② quickly — 빠르게 (동의어)
❌ ③ loudly — 큰 소리로 (의미축이 다름)
❌ ④ clearly — 분명하게 (관련 없음)
det.tip: rapidly growing populations(빠르게 증가하는 인구) ↔ slowly(느리게)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 flammable과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: flammable ↔ fireproof (불이 잘 붙는 ↔ 불에 타지 않는)
det.analysis:
❌ ① toxic — 유독한 (의미축이 다름)
✅ ② fireproof — 불에 타지 않는 ←정답
❌ ③ heavy — 무거운 (관련 없음)
❌ ④ invisible — 보이지 않는 (관련 없음)

questions.passage:
(A) The badly polluted <u>state</u> of the lake worried the scientists. Its water quality had reached a truly dangerous condition.
(B) The <u>state</u> built new roads and schools across the whole region. Its government also funded several large public hospitals.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B) 두 문장에서 밑줄 친 state의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: ③ 상태 — 국가
det.analysis:
✅ ③ (A) the polluted state of the lake는 호수의 '상태'를 뜻하고, (B) The state built roads는 '국가(정부)'를 뜻함 ←정답
❌ ① (A)는 '국가'가 아니라 상태
❌ ② (B)는 '지위'가 아니라 국가
❌ ④ (A)는 '진술하다'가 아니라 상태
det.tip: state: (A) 상태(명사) / (B) 국가·정부(명사)

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"the process by which dead plants and animals are gradually broken down into simpler substances"

det.korean: decomposition (분해, 부패)
det.analysis:
❌ ① purification(정화): 불순물을 제거해 깨끗하게 하는 과정
❌ ② evaporation(증발): 액체가 기체로 변하는 현상
❌ ③ circulation(순환): 무언가가 돌고 도는 것
✅ ④ decomposition(분해): 죽은 동식물이 더 단순한 물질로 분해되는 과정 ←정답
det.tip: decomposition = (유기물의) 분해·부패

questions.passage: The severely degraded state of many urban lakes __________ (highlight) that current approaches to managing water quality across cities have failed. City authorities have not fully understood the problem.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.korean: highlights (3인칭 단수 현재)
det.analysis: highlight(동사 원형) → highlights: 주어 The severely degraded state가 3인칭 단수이므로 현재시제 동사는 highlights가 되어야 한다.
det.tip: 단수 주어 state → highlights (highlight ✕)

questions.passage: Decomposition of this organic matter __________ (lead) to a loss of oxygen from the water and a decline in fish and most other animal life. This happened in the past.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.korean: led (과거시제)
det.analysis: lead(동사 원형) → led: 뒤에 'This happened in the past'로 과거 사실을 서술하므로, 과거시제 불규칙 변화형 led가 되어야 한다. 'led to(~로 이어졌다)'가 맞다.
det.tip: lead-led-led: led to a loss of oxygen(산소 손실로 이어졌다)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 유기물의 분해가 물에서 '산소의 손실(loss of oxygen)'로 이어져 어류와 동물이 감소했다는 흐름이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① loss of oxygen — 산소의 손실 ←정답
❌ ② rise in fish — 어류의 증가 (뒤의 decline in fish와 모순)
❌ ③ gain of nutrients — 영양분의 증가 (분해의 결과로 부적합)
❌ ④ change of color — 색의 변화 (어류 감소의 원인으로 부적합)
det.tip: led to a loss of oxygen ... and a decline in fish = 산소 손실 → 어류 감소

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 오염 규제 담당자들이 산업 폐기물에 주로 집중하고 '가정 폐수(household wastewater)'에는 소홀하다는 흐름이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① clean rivers — 깨끗한 강 (규제 대상 폐기물이 아님)
✅ ② household wastewater — 가정 폐수 ←정답
❌ ③ public parks — 공원 (오염 규제 대상으로 부적합)
❌ ④ drinking water — 식수 (industrial waste와 대비되는 대상으로 부적합)
det.tip: focus on industrial waste rather than household wastewater = 산업 폐기물에 집중, 가정 폐수는 소홀
